dialogue.text: In 1937 Picasso was the most famous artist in the world.
dialogue.zh: In 1937 Picasso was the most famous artist in the world.
dialogue.ja: 1937年、ピカソは世界で最も有名な芸術家でした。
dialogue.local: In 1937 Picasso was the most famous artist in the world.
dialogue.en: In 1937 Picasso was the most famous artist in the world.

dialogue.text: A prolific innovator of art forms, he had already pioneered cubism, invented collage,
dialogue.zh: A prolific innovator of art forms, he had already pioneered cubism, invented collage,
dialogue.ja: 彼は多作な芸術形式の革新者であり、すでにキュビスムを開拓し、コラージュを発明していました。
dialogue.local: A prolific innovator of art forms, he had already pioneered cubism, invented collage,
dialogue.en: A prolific innovator of art forms, he had already pioneered cubism, invented collage,

dialogue.text: and made major contributions to symbolism and surrealism.
dialogue.zh: and made major contributions to symbolism and surrealism.
dialogue.ja: そして象徴主義やシュルレアリスムにも大きな貢献をしました。
dialogue.local: and made major contributions to symbolism and surrealism.
dialogue.en: and made major contributions to symbolism and surrealism.

dialogue.text: And he was just about to create the most powerful anti-war painting in history.
dialogue.zh: And he was just about to create the most powerful anti-war painting in history.
dialogue.ja: そして彼は歴史上最も強力な反戦画をまさに創ろうとしていました。
dialogue.local: And he was just about to create the most powerful anti-war painting in history.
dialogue.en: And he was just about to create the most powerful anti-war painting in history.

dialogue.text: Monday, April the 26th, 1937.
dialogue.zh: Monday, April the 26th, 1937.
dialogue.ja: 1937年4月26日、月曜日。
dialogue.local: Monday, April the 26th, 1937.
dialogue.en: Monday, April the 26th, 1937.

dialogue.text: German warplanes began appearing in the sky above the small busk village of Guernica.
dialogue.zh: German warplanes began appearing in the sky above the small busk village of Guernica.
dialogue.ja: ドイツの戦闘機が小さなバスクの村ゲルニカの上空に現れ始めました。
dialogue.local: German warplanes began appearing in the sky above the small busk village of Guernica.
dialogue.en: German warplanes began appearing in the sky above the small busk village of Guernica.

dialogue.text: It was 4.30pm, and the planes were here on behalf of General Franco's fascist regime,
dialogue.zh: It was 4.30pm, and the planes were here on behalf of General Franco's fascist regime,
dialogue.ja: 午後4時30分で、飛行機はフランコ将軍のファシスト政権を代表していました。
dialogue.local: It was 4.30pm, and the planes were here on behalf of General Franco's fascist regime,
dialogue.en: It was 4.30pm, and the planes were here on behalf of General Franco's fascist regime,

dialogue.text: and as a macabre rehearsal for the Blitzkrieg tactics of World War II.
dialogue.zh: and as a macabre rehearsal for the Blitzkrieg tactics of World War II.
dialogue.ja: そして第二次世界大戦の電撃戦戦術の不気味なリハーサルとしてでした。
dialogue.local: and as a macabre rehearsal for the Blitzkrieg tactics of World War II.
dialogue.en: and as a macabre rehearsal for the Blitzkrieg tactics of World War II.

dialogue.text: The attack was timed to maximize civilian casualties.
dialogue.zh: The attack was timed to maximize civilian casualties.
dialogue.ja: 攻撃は民間人の犠牲者を最大化するために計画されました。
dialogue.local: The attack was timed to maximize civilian casualties.
dialogue.en: The attack was timed to maximize civilian casualties.

dialogue.text: For over three hours, 25 bombers dropped 100,000 pounds of explosive and incendiary bombs on the village,
dialogue.zh: For over three hours, 25 bombers dropped 100,000 pounds of explosive and incendiary bombs on the village,
dialogue.ja: 3時間以上にわたり、25機の爆撃機が村に10万ポンドの爆発物と焼夷弾を投下しました。
dialogue.local: For over three hours, 25 bombers dropped 100,000 pounds of explosive and incendiary bombs on the village,
dialogue.en: For over three hours, 25 bombers dropped 100,000 pounds of explosive and incendiary bombs on the village,

dialogue.text: reducing it to rubble and killing a third of the population.
dialogue.zh: reducing it to rubble and killing a third of the population.
dialogue.ja: 村は瓦礫の山となり、住民の3分の1が死亡しました。
dialogue.local: reducing it to rubble and killing a third of the population.
dialogue.en: reducing it to rubble and killing a third of the population.

dialogue.text: This brutal and unprovoked attack shot the world.
dialogue.zh: This brutal and unprovoked attack shot the world.
dialogue.ja: この残酷で不当な攻撃は世界を震撼させました。
dialogue.local: This brutal and unprovoked attack shot the world.
dialogue.en: This brutal and unprovoked attack shot the world.

dialogue.text: He also inspired Picasso to produce a political painting that is as relevant today as it was when he produced it over 80 years ago.
dialogue.zh: He also inspired Picasso to produce a political painting that is as relevant today as it was when he produced it over 80 years ago.
dialogue.ja: これがピカソに政治的な絵画を制作させ、80年以上前に制作された時と同じくらい今日でも重要な作品となっています。
dialogue.local: He also inspired Picasso to produce a political painting that is as relevant today as it was when he produced it over 80 years ago.
dialogue.en: He also inspired Picasso to produce a political painting that is as relevant today as it was when he produced it over 80 years ago.

dialogue.text: In 1936, a group of right-wing generals launched a military coup on the legally elected Spanish Republic
dialogue.zh: In 1936, a group of right-wing generals launched a military coup on the legally elected Spanish Republic
dialogue.ja: 1936年、右翼の将軍たちが合法的に選ばれたスペイン共和国に対して軍事クーデターを起こしました。
dialogue.local: In 1936, a group of right-wing generals launched a military coup on the legally elected Spanish Republic
dialogue.en: In 1936, a group of right-wing generals launched a military coup on the legally elected Spanish Republic

dialogue.text: and started the Spanish Civil War.
dialogue.zh: and started the Spanish Civil War.
dialogue.ja: そしてスペイン内戦が始まりました。
dialogue.local: and started the Spanish Civil War.
dialogue.en: and started the Spanish Civil War.

dialogue.text: War had been going on for six months when Picasso was given a commission to produce a large-scale mural for the Spanish Republic's pavilion at the 1937 World's Fair in Paris,
dialogue.zh: War had been going on for six months when Picasso was given a commission to produce a large-scale mural for the Spanish Republic's pavilion at the 1937 World's Fair in Paris,
dialogue.ja: 戦争が6か月続いていた時、ピカソは1937年のパリ万国博覧会のスペイン共和国館のために大規模な壁画を制作する依頼を受けました。
dialogue.local: War had been going on for six months when Picasso was given a commission to produce a large-scale mural for the Spanish Republic's pavilion at the 1937 World's Fair in Paris,
dialogue.en: War had been going on for six months when Picasso was given a commission to produce a large-scale mural for the Spanish Republic's pavilion at the 1937 World's Fair in Paris,

dialogue.text: where Picasso was living.
dialogue.zh: where Picasso was living.
dialogue.ja: ピカソはパリに住んでいました。
dialogue.local: where Picasso was living.
dialogue.en: where Picasso was living.

dialogue.text: Picasso was famously apolitical and told the republicans, I don't do politics.
dialogue.zh: Picasso was famously apolitical and told the republicans, I don't do politics.
dialogue.ja: ピカソは政治に関心がないことで有名で、共和派に「私は政治をしない」と言いました。
dialogue.local: Picasso was famously apolitical and told the republicans, I don't do politics.
dialogue.en: Picasso was famously apolitical and told the republicans, I don't do politics.

dialogue.text: But after months of staring at a blank canvas, he was still struggling to come up with ideas.
dialogue.zh: But after months of staring at a blank canvas, he was still struggling to come up with ideas.
dialogue.ja: しかし、数か月間白紙のキャンバスを見つめた後も、彼はまだアイデアを思いつけずにいました。
dialogue.local: But after months of staring at a blank canvas, he was still struggling to come up with ideas.
dialogue.en: But after months of staring at a blank canvas, he was still struggling to come up with ideas.

dialogue.text: History intervened, and Picasso found his subject.
dialogue.zh: History intervened, and Picasso found his subject.
dialogue.ja: 歴史が介入し、ピカソは題材を見つけました。
dialogue.local: History intervened, and Picasso found his subject.
dialogue.en: History intervened, and Picasso found his subject.

dialogue.text: Like the rest of the world, he opened his newspaper on April the 27th to find devastating images of the bombing of Gernica.
dialogue.zh: Like the rest of the world, he opened his newspaper on April the 27th to find devastating images of the bombing of Gernica.
dialogue.ja: 世界中の人々と同様に、彼は4月27日に新聞を開き、ゲルニカ爆撃の壊滅的な映像を目にしました。
dialogue.local: Like the rest of the world, he opened his newspaper on April the 27th to find devastating images of the bombing of Gernica.
dialogue.en: Like the rest of the world, he opened his newspaper on April the 27th to find devastating images of the bombing of Gernica.

dialogue.text: Picasso was horrified and frantically started work on new sketches for the commission.
dialogue.zh: Picasso was horrified and frantically started work on new sketches for the commission.
dialogue.ja: ピカソは恐怖に駆られ、委託作品のための新しいスケッチを必死に描き始めました。
dialogue.local: Picasso was horrified and frantically started work on new sketches for the commission.
dialogue.en: Picasso was horrified and frantically started work on new sketches for the commission.

dialogue.text: He would complete the enormous painting in only three weeks.
dialogue.zh: He would complete the enormous painting in only three weeks.
dialogue.ja: 彼はわずか3週間で巨大な絵画を完成させました。
dialogue.local: He would complete the enormous painting in only three weeks.
dialogue.en: He would complete the enormous painting in only three weeks.

dialogue.text: Perhaps Picasso's greatest skill was reinvention.
dialogue.zh: Perhaps Picasso's greatest skill was reinvention.
dialogue.ja: おそらくピカソの最大の才能は再発明でした。
dialogue.local: Perhaps Picasso's greatest skill was reinvention.
dialogue.en: Perhaps Picasso's greatest skill was reinvention.

dialogue.text: In Le Demois L. Davignon, he played with idealised female beauty,
dialogue.zh: In Le Demois L. Davignon, he played with idealised female beauty,
dialogue.ja: 『ル・デモワゼル・L・ダヴィニョン』では、彼は理想化された女性の美しさを表現しました。
dialogue.local: In Le Demois L. Davignon, he played with idealised female beauty,
dialogue.en: In Le Demois L. Davignon, he played with idealised female beauty,

dialogue.text: and in Gernica, he would reinvigorate the genre of historical painting.
dialogue.zh: and in Gernica, he would reinvigorate the genre of historical painting.
dialogue.ja: そして『ゲルニカ』では、彼は歴史画のジャンルに新たな活力を与えました。
dialogue.local: and in Gernica, he would reinvigorate the genre of historical painting.
dialogue.en: and in Gernica, he would reinvigorate the genre of historical painting.

dialogue.text: The first thing you notice is the gigantic size.
dialogue.zh: The first thing you notice is the gigantic size.
dialogue.ja: 最初に目に入るのはその巨大なサイズです。
dialogue.local: The first thing you notice is the gigantic size.
dialogue.en: The first thing you notice is the gigantic size.

dialogue.text: It is 4 metres by 8 metres, or 11 feet by 26 feet, and is one piece of material rather than several canvases sewn together.
dialogue.zh: It is 4 metres by 8 metres, or 11 feet by 26 feet, and is one piece of material rather than several canvases sewn together.
dialogue.ja: 4メートル×8メートル、または11フィート×26フィートの大きさで、複数のキャンバスを縫い合わせたものではなく、一枚の素材でできています。
dialogue.local: It is 4 metres by 8 metres, or 11 feet by 26 feet, and is one piece of material rather than several canvases sewn together.
dialogue.en: It is 4 metres by 8 metres, or 11 feet by 26 feet, and is one piece of material rather than several canvases sewn together.

dialogue.text: After Paris, it was to be sent around the world to raise money for Spain.
dialogue.zh: After Paris, it was to be sent around the world to raise money for Spain.
dialogue.ja: パリの後、スペインのための資金調達のために世界中を巡回しました。
dialogue.local: After Paris, it was to be sent around the world to raise money for Spain.
dialogue.en: After Paris, it was to be sent around the world to raise money for Spain.

dialogue.text: Because of the size, each time it travelled, the canvas had to be removed from the stretcher, rolled up, packed and shipped.
dialogue.zh: Because of the size, each time it travelled, the canvas had to be removed from the stretcher, rolled up, packed and shipped.
dialogue.ja: サイズのため、移動のたびにキャンバスを張る枠から外し、巻いて梱包し発送しなければなりませんでした。
dialogue.local: Because of the size, each time it travelled, the canvas had to be removed from the stretcher, rolled up, packed and shipped.
dialogue.en: Because of the size, each time it travelled, the canvas had to be removed from the stretcher, rolled up, packed and shipped.

dialogue.text: Again and again.
dialogue.zh: Again and again.
dialogue.ja: 何度も何度も繰り返されました。
dialogue.local: Again and again.
dialogue.en: Again and again.

dialogue.text: In that sense, we can compare Gernica to portable tapestries known in Spain as Sardgas.
dialogue.zh: In that sense, we can compare Gernica to portable tapestries known in Spain as Sardgas.
dialogue.ja: その意味で、『ゲルニカ』はスペインでサルダガスと呼ばれる携帯用のタペストリーに例えられます。
dialogue.local: In that sense, we can compare Gernica to portable tapestries known in Spain as Sardgas.
dialogue.en: In that sense, we can compare Gernica to portable tapestries known in Spain as Sardgas.

dialogue.text: They were used in Spain and other countries from the 15th century as temporary curtains, banners and wall hangings during Lent.
dialogue.zh: They were used in Spain and other countries from the 15th century as temporary curtains, banners and wall hangings during Lent.
dialogue.ja: 15世紀からスペインや他の国々で、四旬節の間の仮設カーテンやバナー、壁掛けとして使われていました。
dialogue.local: They were used in Spain and other countries from the 15th century as temporary curtains, banners and wall hangings during Lent.
dialogue.en: They were used in Spain and other countries from the 15th century as temporary curtains, banners and wall hangings during Lent.

dialogue.text: Like Gernica, it was propaganda, but of a religious kind.
dialogue.zh: Like Gernica, it was propaganda, but of a religious kind.
dialogue.ja: 『ゲルニカ』のように、それはプロパガンダでしたが、宗教的なものでした。
dialogue.local: Like Gernica, it was propaganda, but of a religious kind.
dialogue.en: Like Gernica, it was propaganda, but of a religious kind.

dialogue.text: He primed the canvas with several layers of reflective lead white, an antiquated paint base used by Leonardo da Vinci.
dialogue.zh: He primed the canvas with several layers of reflective lead white, an antiquated paint base used by Leonardo da Vinci.
dialogue.ja: 彼はキャンバスにレオナルド・ダ・ヴィンチが使った古風な塗料である反射性の鉛白を何層も塗りました。
dialogue.local: He primed the canvas with several layers of reflective lead white, an antiquated paint base used by Leonardo da Vinci.
dialogue.en: He primed the canvas with several layers of reflective lead white, an antiquated paint base used by Leonardo da Vinci.

dialogue.text: Picasso wanted a reflective surface to paint on.
dialogue.zh: Picasso wanted a reflective surface to paint on.
dialogue.ja: ピカソは反射する表面に絵を描きたかったのです。
dialogue.local: Picasso wanted a reflective surface to paint on.
dialogue.en: Picasso wanted a reflective surface to paint on.

dialogue.text: The ground layer was important as it was to form part of the composition.
dialogue.zh: The ground layer was important as it was to form part of the composition.
dialogue.ja: 下地の層は構図の一部を形成するため重要でした。
dialogue.local: The ground layer was important as it was to form part of the composition.
dialogue.en: The ground layer was important as it was to form part of the composition.

dialogue.text: He used normal household paint with a minimum amount of gloss, so the white parts of the painting are luminous, whereas the blacks are matte black.
dialogue.zh: He used normal household paint with a minimum amount of gloss, so the white parts of the painting are luminous, whereas the blacks are matte black.
dialogue.ja: 彼は通常の家庭用塗料を使い、光沢を最小限に抑えたため、絵の白い部分は輝き、黒い部分はマットな黒になっています。
dialogue.local: He used normal household paint with a minimum amount of gloss, so the white parts of the painting are luminous, whereas the blacks are matte black.
dialogue.en: He used normal household paint with a minimum amount of gloss, so the white parts of the painting are luminous, whereas the blacks are matte black.

dialogue.text: The speed at which he paints leaves splashes, such as here, and mistakes, adding to the urgency of the painting.
dialogue.zh: The speed at which he paints leaves splashes, such as here, and mistakes, adding to the urgency of the painting.
dialogue.ja: 彼の描く速さは、ここにあるような飛び散りやミスを残し、絵の緊迫感を増しています。
dialogue.local: The speed at which he paints leaves splashes, such as here, and mistakes, adding to the urgency of the painting.
dialogue.en: The speed at which he paints leaves splashes, such as here, and mistakes, adding to the urgency of the painting.

dialogue.text: The other thing you notice straight away is the absence of colour.
dialogue.zh: The other thing you notice straight away is the absence of colour.
dialogue.ja: もう一つすぐに気づくのは色彩の欠如です。
dialogue.local: The other thing you notice straight away is the absence of colour.
dialogue.en: The other thing you notice straight away is the absence of colour.

dialogue.text: But in 1937, people only experienced current events in black and white.
dialogue.zh: But in 1937, people only experienced current events in black and white.
dialogue.ja: しかし1937年、人々はニュースを白黒でしか体験できませんでした。
dialogue.local: But in 1937, people only experienced current events in black and white.
dialogue.en: But in 1937, people only experienced current events in black and white.

dialogue.text: And Gernica was as current as you could get.
dialogue.zh: And Gernica was as current as you could get.
dialogue.ja: そして『ゲルニカ』は当時の最も最新の出来事を表していました。
dialogue.local: And Gernica was as current as you could get.
dialogue.en: And Gernica was as current as you could get.

dialogue.text: Picasso himself saw the Spanish Civil War play out in black and white in newspapers, and he even gives us a suggestion of torn newsprint in the white
dialogue.zh: Picasso himself saw the Spanish Civil War play out in black and white in newspapers, and he even gives us a suggestion of torn newsprint in the white
dialogue.ja: ピカソ自身もスペイン内戦を新聞の白黒写真で見ており、白い部分には破れた新聞紙のような表現もあります。
dialogue.local: Picasso himself saw the Spanish Civil War play out in black and white in newspapers, and he even gives us a suggestion of torn newsprint in the white
dialogue.en: Picasso himself saw the Spanish Civil War play out in black and white in newspapers, and he even gives us a suggestion of torn newsprint in the white

dialogue.text: and newsprint in the horses chainmail.
dialogue.zh: and newsprint in the horses chainmail.
dialogue.ja: そして馬の鎖かたびらには新聞の印刷が表現されています。
dialogue.local: and newsprint in the horses chainmail.
dialogue.en: and newsprint in the horses chainmail.

dialogue.text: Picasso was the magpie of the art world with an encyclopedic knowledge of art history.
dialogue.zh: Picasso was the magpie of the art world with an encyclopedic knowledge of art history.
dialogue.ja: ピカソは芸術界のカササギであり、博識な美術史の知識を持っていました。
dialogue.local: Picasso was the magpie of the art world with an encyclopedic knowledge of art history.
dialogue.en: Picasso was the magpie of the art world with an encyclopedic knowledge of art history.

dialogue.text: With Gernica, it is these visual references that anchor the work.
dialogue.zh: With Gernica, it is these visual references that anchor the work.
dialogue.ja: 『ゲルニカ』では、これらの視覚的な参照が作品の基盤となっています。
dialogue.local: With Gernica, it is these visual references that anchor the work.
dialogue.en: With Gernica, it is these visual references that anchor the work.

dialogue.text: Peter Paul Rubens was an artist Picasso loved, and Rubens painting an allegory showing the effects of war from 1638 is the work that most inspired Picasso's Gernica.
dialogue.zh: Peter Paul Rubens was an artist Picasso loved, and Rubens painting an allegory showing the effects of war from 1638 is the work that most inspired Picasso's Gernica.
dialogue.ja: ピーター・ポール・ルーベンスはピカソが愛した画家で、1638年の戦争の影響を描いた寓意画が『ゲルニカ』に最も影響を与えました。
dialogue.local: Peter Paul Rubens was an artist Picasso loved, and Rubens painting an allegory showing the effects of war from 1638 is the work that most inspired Picasso's Gernica.
dialogue.en: Peter Paul Rubens was an artist Picasso loved, and Rubens painting an allegory showing the effects of war from 1638 is the work that most inspired Picasso's Gernica.

dialogue.text: If we flip Rubens painting, we can see the similarities in composition.
dialogue.zh: If we flip Rubens painting, we can see the similarities in composition.
dialogue.ja: ルーベンスの絵を反転させると、構図の類似点が見られます。
dialogue.local: If we flip Rubens painting, we can see the similarities in composition.
dialogue.en: If we flip Rubens painting, we can see the similarities in composition.

dialogue.text: From left to right, we get a weeping woman with a child in her arms.
dialogue.zh: From left to right, we get a weeping woman with a child in her arms.
dialogue.ja: 左から右へ、子供を抱く泣いている女性がいます。
dialogue.local: From left to right, we get a weeping woman with a child in her arms.
dialogue.en: From left to right, we get a weeping woman with a child in her arms.

dialogue.text: A flying fury of war holding out a torch, and a woman facing the heavens without stretched arms.
dialogue.zh: A flying fury of war holding out a torch, and a woman facing the heavens without stretched arms.
dialogue.ja: 戦争の怒りが松明を掲げ、腕を伸ばさず天を仰ぐ女性がいます。
dialogue.local: A flying fury of war holding out a torch, and a woman facing the heavens without stretched arms.
dialogue.en: A flying fury of war holding out a torch, and a woman facing the heavens without stretched arms.

dialogue.text: We can also compare the weeping woman to Michelangelo's lapierter, and the flying fury to Prudon's allegory of justice.
dialogue.zh: We can also compare the weeping woman to Michelangelo's lapierter, and the flying fury to Prudon's allegory of justice.
dialogue.ja: 泣く女性はミケランジェロの『ラピエール』に、飛ぶ怒りはプリュドンの正義の寓意に例えられます。
dialogue.local: We can also compare the weeping woman to Michelangelo's lapierter, and the flying fury to Prudon's allegory of justice.
dialogue.en: We can also compare the weeping woman to Michelangelo's lapierter, and the flying fury to Prudon's allegory of justice.

dialogue.text: Goya, an artist Picasso admired, is another inspiration.
dialogue.zh: Goya, an artist Picasso admired, is another inspiration.
dialogue.ja: ゴヤはピカソが敬愛した画家で、別のインスピレーションの源です。
dialogue.local: Goya, an artist Picasso admired, is another inspiration.
dialogue.en: Goya, an artist Picasso admired, is another inspiration.

dialogue.text: Third of May 1808 also depicts a nighttime massacre.
dialogue.zh: Third of May 1808 also depicts a nighttime massacre.
dialogue.ja: 『1808年5月3日』も夜の虐殺を描いています。
dialogue.local: Third of May 1808 also depicts a nighttime massacre.
dialogue.en: Third of May 1808 also depicts a nighttime massacre.

dialogue.text: The central figure's pose is reminiscent of the screaming woman, and inevitably, both figures can be compared to a crucifixion.
dialogue.zh: The central figure's pose is reminiscent of the screaming woman, and inevitably, both figures can be compared to a crucifixion.
dialogue.ja: 中央の人物のポーズは叫ぶ女性を思わせ、どちらも十字架の磔刑に例えられます。
dialogue.local: The central figure's pose is reminiscent of the screaming woman, and inevitably, both figures can be compared to a crucifixion.
dialogue.en: The central figure's pose is reminiscent of the screaming woman, and inevitably, both figures can be compared to a crucifixion.

dialogue.text: And in both paintings, we find the sign of the stick martyr.
dialogue.zh: And in both paintings, we find the sign of the stick martyr.
dialogue.ja: 両方の絵に、棒の殉教者のサインが見られます。
dialogue.local: And in both paintings, we find the sign of the stick martyr.
dialogue.en: And in both paintings, we find the sign of the stick martyr.

dialogue.text: There are also comparisons to be made with his own earlier work.
dialogue.zh: There are also comparisons to be made with his own earlier work.
dialogue.ja: 彼自身の初期作品とも比較できます。
dialogue.local: There are also comparisons to be made with his own earlier work.
dialogue.en: There are also comparisons to be made with his own earlier work.

dialogue.text: But there is more than just iconographic inspiration here.
dialogue.zh: But there is more than just iconographic inspiration here.
dialogue.ja: しかし、ここには単なる図像的なインスピレーション以上のものがあります。
dialogue.local: But there is more than just iconographic inspiration here.
dialogue.en: But there is more than just iconographic inspiration here.

dialogue.text: Surprisingly, Picasso's Gernica has no specific references to the actual bombing of the Basque village.
dialogue.zh: Surprisingly, Picasso's Gernica has no specific references to the actual bombing of the Basque village.
dialogue.ja: 驚くべきことに、ピカソの『ゲルニカ』にはバスクの村の実際の爆撃への具体的な言及はありません。
dialogue.local: Surprisingly, Picasso's Gernica has no specific references to the actual bombing of the Basque village.
dialogue.en: Surprisingly, Picasso's Gernica has no specific references to the actual bombing of the Basque village.

dialogue.text: He has created a fictitious scene whose intensity evokes the suffering of all wars.
dialogue.zh: He has created a fictitious scene whose intensity evokes the suffering of all wars.
dialogue.ja: 彼は架空の場面を作り出し、その激しさがすべての戦争の苦しみを呼び起こします。
dialogue.local: He has created a fictitious scene whose intensity evokes the suffering of all wars.
dialogue.en: He has created a fictitious scene whose intensity evokes the suffering of all wars.

dialogue.text: Gernica is an allegorical painting.
dialogue.zh: Gernica is an allegorical painting.
dialogue.ja: 『ゲルニカ』は寓意画です。
dialogue.local: Gernica is an allegorical painting.
dialogue.en: Gernica is an allegorical painting.

dialogue.text: In the same way Rubens work is an allegorical response to the Thirty Years' War.
dialogue.zh: In the same way Rubens work is an allegorical response to the Thirty Years' War.
dialogue.ja: ルーベンスの作品が三十年戦争への寓意的な応答であるのと同様です。
dialogue.local: In the same way Rubens work is an allegorical response to the Thirty Years' War.
dialogue.en: In the same way Rubens work is an allegorical response to the Thirty Years' War.

dialogue.text: The scene is intentionally chaotic to evoke the horror and confusion of war.
dialogue.zh: The scene is intentionally chaotic to evoke the horror and confusion of war.
dialogue.ja: この場面は戦争の恐怖と混乱を呼び起こすために意図的に混沌としています。
dialogue.local: The scene is intentionally chaotic to evoke the horror and confusion of war.
dialogue.en: The scene is intentionally chaotic to evoke the horror and confusion of war.

dialogue.text: We are thrown into apocalyptic action by characters overlap and intersect.
dialogue.zh: We are thrown into apocalyptic action by characters overlap and intersect.
dialogue.ja: 登場人物が重なり合い交差することで、私たちは黙示録的な行動に投げ込まれます。
dialogue.local: We are thrown into apocalyptic action by characters overlap and intersect.
dialogue.en: We are thrown into apocalyptic action by characters overlap and intersect.

dialogue.text: Destruction, violent death, and mutilation are everywhere.
dialogue.zh: Destruction, violent death, and mutilation are everywhere.
dialogue.ja: 破壊、激しい死、そして切断が至る所にあります。
dialogue.local: Destruction, violent death, and mutilation are everywhere.
dialogue.en: Destruction, violent death, and mutilation are everywhere.

dialogue.text: Despite Picasso's avant-garde qualities, he trained as a classical artist.
dialogue.zh: Despite Picasso's avant-garde qualities, he trained as a classical artist.
dialogue.ja: ピカソは前衛的な特徴を持ちながらも、古典的な芸術家として訓練を受けました。
dialogue.local: Despite Picasso's avant-garde qualities, he trained as a classical artist.
dialogue.en: Despite Picasso's avant-garde qualities, he trained as a classical artist.

dialogue.text: And Gernica uses classical language.
dialogue.zh: And Gernica uses classical language.
dialogue.ja: そして『ゲルニカ』は古典的な表現を用いています。
dialogue.local: And Gernica uses classical language.
dialogue.en: And Gernica uses classical language.

dialogue.text: Despite the chaos, there is in fact a clear visual order.
dialogue.zh: Despite the chaos, there is in fact a clear visual order.
dialogue.ja: 混沌の中にも明確な視覚的秩序があります。
dialogue.local: Despite the chaos, there is in fact a clear visual order.
dialogue.en: Despite the chaos, there is in fact a clear visual order.

dialogue.text: Picasso balances the composition by organizing the figures into three vertical groupings, moving left to right.
dialogue.zh: Picasso balances the composition by organizing the figures into three vertical groupings, moving left to right.
dialogue.ja: ピカソは人物を左から右へ三つの縦のグループに分けて構図のバランスをとっています。
dialogue.local: Picasso balances the composition by organizing the figures into three vertical groupings, moving left to right.
dialogue.en: Picasso balances the composition by organizing the figures into three vertical groupings, moving left to right.

dialogue.text: While the central figures are stabilized within a large triangle of light.
dialogue.zh: While the central figures are stabilized within a large triangle of light.
dialogue.ja: 中央の人物は大きな光の三角形の中で安定しています。
dialogue.local: While the central figures are stabilized within a large triangle of light.
dialogue.en: While the central figures are stabilized within a large triangle of light.

dialogue.text: To the far left we see a wide-eyed bull with a dark body and white head.
dialogue.zh: To the far left we see a wide-eyed bull with a dark body and white head.
dialogue.ja: 一番左には、目を見開いた黒い体と白い頭の雄牛がいます。
dialogue.local: To the far left we see a wide-eyed bull with a dark body and white head.
dialogue.en: To the far left we see a wide-eyed bull with a dark body and white head.

dialogue.text: The horse and bull are images Picasso used his entire career, part of the life and death ritual of Spanish bullfights.
dialogue.zh: The horse and bull are images Picasso used his entire career, part of the life and death ritual of Spanish bullfights.
dialogue.ja: 馬と雄牛はピカソが生涯にわたり使ったイメージで、スペインの闘牛の生と死の儀式の一部です。
dialogue.local: The horse and bull are images Picasso used his entire career, part of the life and death ritual of Spanish bullfights.
dialogue.en: The horse and bull are images Picasso used his entire career, part of the life and death ritual of Spanish bullfights.

dialogue.text: The bull is the only figure that is looking at us, the viewer.
dialogue.zh: The bull is the only figure that is looking at us, the viewer.
dialogue.ja: 雄牛は私たち観客を見つめる唯一の人物です。
dialogue.local: The bull is the only figure that is looking at us, the viewer.
dialogue.en: The bull is the only figure that is looking at us, the viewer.

dialogue.text: Picasso himself thought of the bull as representing brutality and darkness.
dialogue.zh: Picasso himself thought of the bull as representing brutality and darkness.
dialogue.ja: ピカソ自身は雄牛を残虐さと闇の象徴と考えていました。
dialogue.local: Picasso himself thought of the bull as representing brutality and darkness.
dialogue.en: Picasso himself thought of the bull as representing brutality and darkness.

dialogue.text: Days is cold and detached.
dialogue.zh: Days is cold and detached.
dialogue.ja: それは冷たく、距離を置いています。
dialogue.local: Days is cold and detached.
dialogue.en: Days is cold and detached.

dialogue.text: It has come to be seen as representing fascism or Franco himself.
dialogue.zh: It has come to be seen as representing fascism or Franco himself.
dialogue.ja: それはファシズムやフランコ自身を象徴すると見なされています。
dialogue.local: It has come to be seen as representing fascism or Franco himself.
dialogue.en: It has come to be seen as representing fascism or Franco himself.

dialogue.text: It's tale smolders like the smoking remains of Gernica.
dialogue.zh: It's tale smolders like the smoking remains of Gernica.
dialogue.ja: その尾はゲルニカの煙る残骸のように燻っています。
dialogue.local: It's tale smolders like the smoking remains of Gernica.
dialogue.en: It's tale smolders like the smoking remains of Gernica.

dialogue.text: Underneath the bull, a woman is holding a dead child, screaming towards the heavens.
dialogue.zh: Underneath the bull, a woman is holding a dead child, screaming towards the heavens.
dialogue.ja: 雄牛の下には、死んだ子供を抱き、天に向かって叫ぶ女性がいます。
dialogue.local: Underneath the bull, a woman is holding a dead child, screaming towards the heavens.
dialogue.en: Underneath the bull, a woman is holding a dead child, screaming towards the heavens.

dialogue.text: Her bare breasts that once fed her child are exposed, and her eyes are in the shape of tears.
dialogue.zh: Her bare breasts that once fed her child are exposed, and her eyes are in the shape of tears.
dialogue.ja: かつて子供に授乳していた裸の胸が露出し、目は涙の形をしています。
dialogue.local: Her bare breasts that once fed her child are exposed, and her eyes are in the shape of tears.
dialogue.en: Her bare breasts that once fed her child are exposed, and her eyes are in the shape of tears.

dialogue.text: She is a secular virgin and child tainted by war.
dialogue.zh: She is a secular virgin and child tainted by war.
dialogue.ja: 彼女は戦争に汚された世俗の聖母と子供です。
dialogue.local: She is a secular virgin and child tainted by war.
dialogue.en: She is a secular virgin and child tainted by war.

dialogue.text: Further down lies a dead soldier, representing both futility and hope.
dialogue.zh: Further down lies a dead soldier, representing both futility and hope.
dialogue.ja: さらに下には死んだ兵士が横たわり、無意味さと希望の両方を表しています。
dialogue.local: Further down lies a dead soldier, representing both futility and hope.
dialogue.en: Further down lies a dead soldier, representing both futility and hope.

dialogue.text: His disjointed parts are strewn about the floor.
dialogue.zh: His disjointed parts are strewn about the floor.
dialogue.ja: 彼のバラバラになった体の部分が床に散らばっています。
dialogue.local: His disjointed parts are strewn about the floor.
dialogue.en: His disjointed parts are strewn about the floor.

dialogue.text: One severed arm carries a broken sword of failure, from which grows a white poppy.
dialogue.zh: One severed arm carries a broken sword of failure, from which grows a white poppy.
dialogue.ja: 一本切断された腕が失敗の折れた剣を持っており、その剣から白いケシの花が咲いています。
dialogue.local: One severed arm carries a broken sword of failure, from which grows a white poppy.
dialogue.en: One severed arm carries a broken sword of failure, from which grows a white poppy.

dialogue.text: The symbol of remembrance and hope.
dialogue.zh: The symbol of remembrance and hope.
dialogue.ja: それは記憶と希望の象徴です。
dialogue.local: The symbol of remembrance and hope.
dialogue.en: The symbol of remembrance and hope.

dialogue.text: In his other hand, the signs of the stigmata represent the ultimate sacrifice.
dialogue.zh: In his other hand, the signs of the stigmata represent the ultimate sacrifice.
dialogue.ja: もう一方の手には、聖痕の印が究極の犠牲を表しています。
dialogue.local: In his other hand, the signs of the stigmata represent the ultimate sacrifice.
dialogue.en: In his other hand, the signs of the stigmata represent the ultimate sacrifice.

dialogue.text: Between the bull and the horse, we can just about see a dove.
dialogue.zh: Between the bull and the horse, we can just about see a dove.
dialogue.ja: 雄牛と馬の間に、かろうじて鳩が見えます。
dialogue.local: Between the bull and the horse, we can just about see a dove.
dialogue.en: Between the bull and the horse, we can just about see a dove.

dialogue.text: Normally a representation of peace, Picasso's version with its pained expression and broken body suggests that pieces all but destroyed.
dialogue.zh: Normally a representation of peace, Picasso's version with its pained expression and broken body suggests that pieces all but destroyed.
dialogue.ja: 通常は平和の象徴である鳩ですが、ピカソの作品では痛ましい表情と壊れた体で、ほとんど破壊された断片を示しています。
dialogue.local: Normally a representation of peace, Picasso's version with its pained expression and broken body suggests that pieces all but destroyed.
dialogue.en: Normally a representation of peace, Picasso's version with its pained expression and broken body suggests that pieces all but destroyed.

dialogue.text: The light bulb is the single image of 20th century technology and has multiple meanings.
dialogue.zh: The light bulb is the single image of 20th century technology and has multiple meanings.
dialogue.ja: 電球は20世紀の技術の象徴であり、複数の意味を持っています。
dialogue.local: The light bulb is the single image of 20th century technology and has multiple meanings.
dialogue.en: The light bulb is the single image of 20th century technology and has multiple meanings.

dialogue.text: Perhaps it is the eye of God overlooking the madness of war.
dialogue.zh: Perhaps it is the eye of God overlooking the madness of war.
dialogue.ja: おそらくそれは戦争の狂気を見下ろす神の目でしょう。
dialogue.local: Perhaps it is the eye of God overlooking the madness of war.
dialogue.en: Perhaps it is the eye of God overlooking the madness of war.

dialogue.text: The more accepted interpretation is that it represents the technology that destroyed Gernica.
dialogue.zh: The more accepted interpretation is that it represents the technology that destroyed Gernica.
dialogue.ja: より一般的な解釈は、それがゲルニカを破壊した技術を表しているということです。
dialogue.local: The more accepted interpretation is that it represents the technology that destroyed Gernica.
dialogue.en: The more accepted interpretation is that it represents the technology that destroyed Gernica.

dialogue.text: In Spanish, the word for light bulb is bombia, which brings to mind the word bomb.
dialogue.zh: In Spanish, the word for light bulb is bombia, which brings to mind the word bomb.
dialogue.ja: スペイン語で電球は「bombia」と言い、爆弾を連想させます。
dialogue.local: In Spanish, the word for light bulb is bombia, which brings to mind the word bomb.
dialogue.en: In Spanish, the word for light bulb is bombia, which brings to mind the word bomb.

dialogue.text: The screaming horse at the center is collapsing from its gaping wound, but its head remains upward as it struggles to live.
dialogue.zh: The screaming horse at the center is collapsing from its gaping wound, but its head remains upward as it struggles to live.
dialogue.ja: 中央の叫んでいる馬は大きな傷から倒れていますが、頭は上を向いたまま生きようとしています。
dialogue.local: The screaming horse at the center is collapsing from its gaping wound, but its head remains upward as it struggles to live.
dialogue.en: The screaming horse at the center is collapsing from its gaping wound, but its head remains upward as it struggles to live.

dialogue.text: You can almost hear those ear piercing screams.
dialogue.zh: You can almost hear those ear piercing screams.
dialogue.ja: その耳をつんざくような叫び声がほとんど聞こえるようです。
dialogue.local: You can almost hear those ear piercing screams.
dialogue.en: You can almost hear those ear piercing screams.

dialogue.text: Picasso himself saw the terrorized horse as the people of Gernica.
dialogue.zh: Picasso himself saw the terrorized horse as the people of Gernica.
dialogue.ja: ピカソ自身は恐怖におののく馬をゲルニカの人々と見なしました。
dialogue.local: Picasso himself saw the terrorized horse as the people of Gernica.
dialogue.en: Picasso himself saw the terrorized horse as the people of Gernica.

dialogue.text: The burning woman is perhaps the strongest representation of the painting's anti-war feeling.
dialogue.zh: The burning woman is perhaps the strongest representation of the painting's anti-war feeling.
dialogue.ja: 燃えている女性は、この絵の反戦感情を最も強く表現しているかもしれません。
dialogue.local: The burning woman is perhaps the strongest representation of the painting's anti-war feeling.
dialogue.en: The burning woman is perhaps the strongest representation of the painting's anti-war feeling.

dialogue.text: A woman is trapped in a burning building, pleading at the sky, perhaps to God, perhaps to the German planes to stop the destruction.
dialogue.zh: A woman is trapped in a burning building, pleading at the sky, perhaps to God, perhaps to the German planes to stop the destruction.
dialogue.ja: 女性が燃える建物に閉じ込められ、空に懇願しています。おそらく神に、あるいはドイツの飛行機に破壊をやめるように。
dialogue.local: A woman is trapped in a burning building, pleading at the sky, perhaps to God, perhaps to the German planes to stop the destruction.
dialogue.en: A woman is trapped in a burning building, pleading at the sky, perhaps to God, perhaps to the German planes to stop the destruction.

dialogue.text: As she does so, the building continues to burn and crumble around her.
dialogue.zh: As she does so, the building continues to burn and crumble around her.
dialogue.ja: 彼女がそうしている間も、建物は彼女の周りで燃え続け、崩れています。
dialogue.local: As she does so, the building continues to burn and crumble around her.
dialogue.en: As she does so, the building continues to burn and crumble around her.

dialogue.text: Death is inevitable.
dialogue.zh: Death is inevitable.
dialogue.ja: 死は避けられません。
dialogue.local: Death is inevitable.
dialogue.en: Death is inevitable.

dialogue.text: Another terrified woman with an injured leg bleeding from the knee and trying to stop the blood with her hand.
dialogue.zh: Another terrified woman with an injured leg bleeding from the knee and trying to stop the blood with her hand.
dialogue.ja: もう一人の恐怖におののく女性は、膝から出血している負傷した脚を手で止めようとしています。
dialogue.local: Another terrified woman with an injured leg bleeding from the knee and trying to stop the blood with her hand.
dialogue.en: Another terrified woman with an injured leg bleeding from the knee and trying to stop the blood with her hand.

dialogue.text: She is looking longingly towards the oil lamp.
dialogue.zh: She is looking longingly towards the oil lamp.
dialogue.ja: 彼女は切望するように油灯の方を見ています。
dialogue.local: She is looking longingly towards the oil lamp.
dialogue.en: She is looking longingly towards the oil lamp.

dialogue.text: It is actually the oil lamp that is the source of light in the scene, and not the electric light bulb.
dialogue.zh: It is actually the oil lamp that is the source of light in the scene, and not the electric light bulb.
dialogue.ja: 実際には、この場面の光源は電球ではなく油灯です。
dialogue.local: It is actually the oil lamp that is the source of light in the scene, and not the electric light bulb.
dialogue.en: It is actually the oil lamp that is the source of light in the scene, and not the electric light bulb.

dialogue.text: The tiny flame is hope, and it is strong enough to shed light upon the entire scene.
dialogue.zh: The tiny flame is hope, and it is strong enough to shed light upon the entire scene.
dialogue.ja: 小さな炎は希望であり、場面全体を照らすのに十分な強さです。
dialogue.local: The tiny flame is hope, and it is strong enough to shed light upon the entire scene.
dialogue.en: The tiny flame is hope, and it is strong enough to shed light upon the entire scene.

dialogue.text: It is the only sliver of hope in the painting, and is thought to represent the spirit of the Spanish Republic.
dialogue.zh: It is the only sliver of hope in the painting, and is thought to represent the spirit of the Spanish Republic.
dialogue.ja: それは絵画の中で唯一の希望のかけらであり、スペイン共和国の精神を表していると考えられています。
dialogue.local: It is the only sliver of hope in the painting, and is thought to represent the spirit of the Spanish Republic.
dialogue.en: It is the only sliver of hope in the painting, and is thought to represent the spirit of the Spanish Republic.

dialogue.text: Gernica is not supposed to have a singular interpretation.
dialogue.zh: Gernica is not supposed to have a singular interpretation.
dialogue.ja: ゲルニカは一つの解釈だけを持つべきではありません。
dialogue.local: Gernica is not supposed to have a singular interpretation.
dialogue.en: Gernica is not supposed to have a singular interpretation.

dialogue.text: As Picasso said, we all know that art is not truth.
dialogue.zh: As Picasso said, we all know that art is not truth.
dialogue.ja: ピカソが言ったように、私たちは皆、芸術が真実ではないことを知っています。
dialogue.local: As Picasso said, we all know that art is not truth.
dialogue.en: As Picasso said, we all know that art is not truth.

dialogue.text: Art is a lie that makes us realise truth.
dialogue.zh: Art is a lie that makes us realise truth.
dialogue.ja: 芸術は私たちに真実を気づかせる嘘です。
dialogue.local: Art is a lie that makes us realise truth.
dialogue.en: Art is a lie that makes us realise truth.

dialogue.text: Gernica's ambiguity and lack of specific historical detail make the painting timeless.
dialogue.zh: Gernica's ambiguity and lack of specific historical detail make the painting timeless.
dialogue.ja: ゲルニカの曖昧さと具体的な歴史的詳細の欠如が、この絵を時代を超えたものにしています。
dialogue.local: Gernica's ambiguity and lack of specific historical detail make the painting timeless.
dialogue.en: Gernica's ambiguity and lack of specific historical detail make the painting timeless.

dialogue.text: Picasso worked on the painting for 35 days, and finished it on the 4th June 1937.
dialogue.zh: Picasso worked on the painting for 35 days, and finished it on the 4th June 1937.
dialogue.ja: ピカソはこの絵に35日間取り組み、1937年6月4日に完成させました。
dialogue.local: Picasso worked on the painting for 35 days, and finished it on the 4th June 1937.
dialogue.en: Picasso worked on the painting for 35 days, and finished it on the 4th June 1937.

dialogue.text: When it was unveiled at the Paris Expo, the public reaction was mixed.
dialogue.zh: When it was unveiled at the Paris Expo, the public reaction was mixed.
dialogue.ja: パリ万博で公開されたとき、一般の反応は賛否両論でした。
dialogue.local: When it was unveiled at the Paris Expo, the public reaction was mixed.
dialogue.en: When it was unveiled at the Paris Expo, the public reaction was mixed.

dialogue.text: It was two avant-garde for the Spanish officials who preferred another more traditional painting that they had also commissioned.
dialogue.zh: It was two avant-garde for the Spanish officials who preferred another more traditional painting that they had also commissioned.
dialogue.ja: それはスペインの役人にはあまりにも前衛的すぎて、彼らは別のより伝統的な絵画を好み、それも委託していました。
dialogue.local: It was two avant-garde for the Spanish officials who preferred another more traditional painting that they had also commissioned.
dialogue.en: It was two avant-garde for the Spanish officials who preferred another more traditional painting that they had also commissioned.

dialogue.text: By Haudacio Ferre de Mogado.
dialogue.zh: By Haudacio Ferre de Mogado.
dialogue.ja: ハウダシオ・フェレ・デ・モガドによる作品です。
dialogue.local: By Haudacio Ferre de Mogado.
dialogue.en: By Haudacio Ferre de Mogado.

dialogue.text: However, after Paris, Gernica's reputation started to grow steadily as it travelled the world to raise money for the Republican cause.
dialogue.zh: However, after Paris, Gernica's reputation started to grow steadily as it travelled the world to raise money for the Republican cause.
dialogue.ja: しかし、パリの後、ゲルニカの評判は共和党のための資金を集めるために世界を巡るにつれて着実に高まり始めました。
dialogue.local: However, after Paris, Gernica's reputation started to grow steadily as it travelled the world to raise money for the Republican cause.
dialogue.en: However, after Paris, Gernica's reputation started to grow steadily as it travelled the world to raise money for the Republican cause.

dialogue.text: The start of the Second World War made its imagery more recognisable and painfully familiar.
dialogue.zh: The start of the Second World War made its imagery more recognisable and painfully familiar.
dialogue.ja: 第二次世界大戦の始まりは、そのイメージをより認識しやすく、痛ましいほど馴染み深いものにしました。
dialogue.local: The start of the Second World War made its imagery more recognisable and painfully familiar.
dialogue.en: The start of the Second World War made its imagery more recognisable and painfully familiar.

dialogue.text: Picasso refused to allow the painting to be seen in Spain while Franco ruled, and Gernica was sent on another tour.
dialogue.zh: Picasso refused to allow the painting to be seen in Spain while Franco ruled, and Gernica was sent on another tour.
dialogue.ja: フランコが支配している間、ピカソはこの絵がスペインで見られることを拒否し、ゲルニカは別の巡回展に送られました。
dialogue.local: Picasso refused to allow the painting to be seen in Spain while Franco ruled, and Gernica was sent on another tour.
dialogue.en: Picasso refused to allow the painting to be seen in Spain while Franco ruled, and Gernica was sent on another tour.

dialogue.text: This time to the United States to raise money for Spanish refugees fleeing fascism.
dialogue.zh: This time to the United States to raise money for Spanish refugees fleeing fascism.
dialogue.ja: 今回はファシズムから逃れるスペイン難民のために資金を集めるためにアメリカ合衆国へ送り出されました。
dialogue.local: This time to the United States to raise money for Spanish refugees fleeing fascism.
dialogue.en: This time to the United States to raise money for Spanish refugees fleeing fascism.

dialogue.text: By 1940, it was at the Museum of Modern Art in New York, where it stayed on semi-permanent display.
dialogue.zh: By 1940, it was at the Museum of Modern Art in New York, where it stayed on semi-permanent display.
dialogue.ja: 1940年までに、それはニューヨークの近代美術館にあり、そこで半永久的に展示されました。
dialogue.local: By 1940, it was at the Museum of Modern Art in New York, where it stayed on semi-permanent display.
dialogue.en: By 1940, it was at the Museum of Modern Art in New York, where it stayed on semi-permanent display.

dialogue.text: For the next 40 years.
dialogue.zh: For the next 40 years.
dialogue.ja: その後の40年間です。
dialogue.local: For the next 40 years.
dialogue.en: For the next 40 years.

dialogue.text: Picasso continued living in Nazi-occupied Paris.
dialogue.zh: Picasso continued living in Nazi-occupied Paris.
